title: Central cache server and client sync architecture
answers: How does thinker sync work end to end?
Where is the sync server code?
How do agent sessions get streamed to the central cache?
Where is the GitHub Action for PR ingestion?
How does deployment of the sync server work?
body: Server lives in `src/server/` (bin `thinker-server`): `index.js` is the HTTP API (notes pull by cursor, note push with conflict detection, session streaming, PR ingest, repos/tokens); `repos.js` holds one `Store` + git clone + numbered change journal per repository; `worker.js` runs background distill/maintain on a daily spend cap; `auth.js` hashes tokens and scopes them by repo and read/write/admin. Client side is `src/sync.js` (`thinker sync login/pull/push`, stream session) wired into `src/cli.js` (`sync` subcommand, prompt-hook background pull every 5min, stop-hook streams session instead of local distill) and `src/maintain.js` (pulls/pushes each maintenance run; disables local PR mining once synced). CI ingestion is `action/ingest.mjs` + `action/action.yml`, posting PR diff/comments to the server; `src/prs.js` reads comments from the payload when CI supplies them instead of calling `gh`. Deployment is `infra/sync/{stack.yaml,deploy.mjs,bootstrap.sh,production.json}` — CloudFormation + EC2 (t4g.small, Caddy, SSM) — never auto-run by the agent.
